solutions.title: Taylor series of sine
solutions.body:
$\sin x=x-\frac{x^3}{3!}+\frac{x^5}{5!}-\cdots$. At $x=1$ the series is exactly $1-\frac1{3!}+\frac1{5!}-\cdots$, so the value is $\sin1$.

**Answer: $\sin 1$**

solutions.title: Imaginary part of $e^{i}$
solutions.body:
$e^{i}=\sum\frac{i^k}{k!}=\left(1-\frac1{2!}+\frac1{4!}-\cdots\right)+i\left(1-\frac1{3!}+\frac1{5!}-\cdots\right)$, and $e^i=\cos1+i\sin1$. Comparing imaginary parts, the series equals $\sin1\approx0.8415$.

**Answer: $\sin 1$**

prompt: At RMT 2009 is a man named Bill who has an infinite amount of time. This year, he is walking continuously at a speed of $\dfrac1{1+t^2}$, starting at time $t=0$. If he continues to walk for an infinite amount of time, how far will he walk?

solutions.title: Integrate the speed
solutions.body:
Distance $=\int_0^\infty\frac{dt}{1+t^2}=\lim_{b\to\infty}\arctan b-\arctan0=\frac\pi2$.

**Answer: $\frac\pi2$**

solutions.title: Substitution
solutions.body:
Let $t=\tan\theta$, $dt=\sec^2\theta\,d\theta$, $1+t^2=\sec^2\theta$. As $t$ goes from $0$ to $\infty$, $\theta$ goes from $0$ to $\frac\pi2$, so the integral is $\int_0^{\pi/2}d\theta=\frac\pi2$.

**Answer: $\frac\pi2$**

solutions.title: Standard limit
solutions.body:
$\frac{10x^2}{\sin^2 3x}=\frac{10}{9}\left(\frac{3x}{\sin3x}\right)^2\to\frac{10}9\cdot1=\frac{10}9$.

**Answer: $\frac{10}{9}$**

solutions.title: L'Hopital
solutions.body:
Differentiating numerator and denominator: $\frac{20x}{6\sin3x\cos3x}=\frac{20x}{3\sin6x}$. Both still tend to $0$; differentiate again: $\frac{20}{18\cos6x}\to\frac{10}{9}$.

**Answer: $\frac{10}{9}$**

solutions.title: Integration by parts
solutions.body:
With $u=\tan^{-1}x$, $dv=dx$:
$$\int_0^1\tan^{-1}x\,dx=\Big[x\tan^{-1}x\Big]_0^1-\int_0^1\frac{x}{1+x^2}dx=\frac\pi4-\frac12\ln2.$$

**Answer: $\frac\pi4-\frac{\ln2}2$**

solutions.title: Area interpretation
solutions.body:
The integral is the area under $y=\tan^{-1}x$ on $[0,1]$. The rectangle $[0,1]\times[0,\frac\pi4]$ has area $\frac\pi4$, and the area to the left of the curve inside it is $\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan y\,dy=-\ln\cos\frac\pi4=\frac12\ln2$. So the area under the curve is $\frac\pi4-\frac{\ln2}2\approx0.4388$.

**Answer: $\frac\pi4-\frac{\ln2}2$**

prompt: Let $a(t)=\cos^2(2t)$ be the acceleration at time $t$ of a point particle traveling on a straight line. Suppose at time $t=0$, the particle is at position $x=1$ with velocity $v=-2$. Find its position at time $t=2$.

solutions.title: Double-integral formula
solutions.body:
$x(t)=x_0+v_0t+\int_0^t(t-s)a(s)\,ds$. For $t=2$: $1-4+\int_0^2(2-s)\cos^22s\,ds$. The integral equals $\int_0^2(2-s)\frac{1+\cos4s}2ds=\left[\,2s-\frac{s^2}{2}\right]_0^2\cdot\frac12+\frac12\int_0^2(2-s)\cos4s\,ds=1+\frac12\cdot\frac{1-\cos8}{16}$, so $x(2)=-3+1+\frac{1-\cos8}{32}=-\frac{63+\cos8}{32}$. A numerical integration also gives $-1.9642$.

**Answer: $-\dfrac{63+\cos 8}{32}$**

reviewNote: Official key gives (33-cos 8)/32, which drops the t^2/4-2t terms of the position at t=2; the correct value -(63+cos 8)/32 (about -1.964) was confirmed by numerical integration.

solutions.title: Geometric series
solutions.body:
$\frac{d^n}{dx^n}e^{-ax}=(-a)^ne^{-ax}$, so the sum is $e^{-ax}\sum_{n\ge2}(-a)^n=e^{-ax}\cdot\frac{a^2}{1-(-a)}=\frac{a^2}{1+a}e^{-ax}$, valid since $|-a|<1$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{a^2}{1+a}e^{-ax}$**

solutions.title: Subtract the first terms
solutions.body:
The full sum $\sum_{n\ge0}(-a)^n=\frac1{1+a}$; remove $n=0,1$: $\frac1{1+a}-1+a=\frac{1-(1+a)(1-a)}{1+a}=\frac{a^2}{1+a}$. Multiply by $e^{-ax}$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{a^2}{1+a}e^{-ax}$**

solutions.title: Riemann sum
solutions.body:
The sum is $\sum_{k=1}^n\frac1n\left(1-\frac kn\right)\cos\frac{4k}n$, a right Riemann sum for $\int_0^1(1-y)\cos4y\,dy$. By parts,
$$\int_0^1(1-y)\cos4y\,dy=\Big[(1-y)\tfrac{\sin4y}{4}\Big]_0^1+\frac14\int_0^1\sin4y\,dy=\frac{1-\cos4}{16}.$$

**Answer: $\dfrac{1-\cos4}{16}$**

solutions.title: Numerical check
solutions.body:
For $n=2\cdot10^6$ the sum is $0.103352\ldots$ and $\frac{1-\cos4}{16}=0.103352\ldots$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{1-\cos4}{16}$**

prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^\infty4\lfloor x+7\rfloor e^{-2x}\,dx$. Remember to express your answer as a single fraction.

solutions.title: Split into unit intervals
solutions.body:
On $[k,k+1)$, $\lfloor x+7\rfloor=k+7$ and $\int_k^{k+1}e^{-2x}dx=\frac{e^{-2k}-e^{-2k-2}}2$. So the integral is $\sum_{k\ge0}2(k+7)\left(e^{-2k}-e^{-2k-2}\right)$. Collecting the coefficient of $e^{-2k}$: for $k=0$ it is $14$; for $k\ge1$ it is $2(k+7)-2(k+6)=2$. Hence
$$14+2\sum_{k\ge1}e^{-2k}=12+\frac2{1-e^{-2}}=\frac{14e^2-12}{e^2-1}.$$

**Answer: $\dfrac{14e^2-12}{e^2-1}$**

solutions.title: Write $\lfloor x+7\rfloor=7+\lfloor x\rfloor$
solutions.body:
$\int_0^\infty4\cdot7e^{-2x}dx=14$. And $\int_0^\infty4\lfloor x\rfloor e^{-2x}dx=\sum_{m\ge1}\int_m^\infty4e^{-2x}dx=\sum_{m\ge1}2e^{-2m}=\frac{2e^{-2}}{1-e^{-2}}=\frac{2}{e^2-1}$. Total: $14+\frac2{e^2-1}=\frac{14e^2-12}{e^2-1}\approx14.313$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{14e^2-12}{e^2-1}$**

solutions.title: Shift trick
solutions.body:
Let $S=\sum n5^{-n}$. Then $\frac S5=\sum n5^{-n-1}=\sum(n+1)5^{-n-1}-\sum5^{-n-1}=S-\frac{1/5}{1-1/5}=S-\frac14$. So $\frac{4S}{5}=\frac14$ and $S=\frac5{16}$.

**Answer: $\frac5{16}$**

prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac1{50+n^2/80000}$ as a decimal to the nearest tenth.

solutions.title: Compare with an integral
solutions.body:
The terms decrease in $n$, so
$$\int_1^\infty\frac{dx}{50+x^2/80000}\le\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac1{50+n^2/80000}\le\int_0^\infty\frac{dx}{50+x^2/80000}.$$
Since $50+\frac{x^2}{80000}=50\left(1+\left(\frac{x}{2000}\right)^2\right)$, the right integral equals $\frac{2000}{50}\left[\tan^{-1}u\right]_0^\infty=40\cdot\frac\pi2=20\pi\approx62.83$. The difference between the two bounds is at most the first term $\frac1{50}=0.02$, so the sum lies in $[62.81,62.84]$, which rounds to $62.8$.

**Answer: 62.8**

solutions.title: Computer check
solutions.body:
Summing numerically (about $5\cdot10^6$ terms) gives $62.806$, and the neglected tail is about $\int_{5\cdot10^6}^\infty\frac{80000}{x^2}dx=0.016$, so the sum is $\approx62.822\to62.8$.

**Answer: 62.8**
